sticker_location: No sticker needed. Faucet brands are stamped on the base or the handle.

plan.diagnosis: Hair and soap wrap around the drain stopper's rod right under the drain, and that is what slows almost every bathroom sink. Pulling the stopper and cleaning it fixes most of them in five minutes, no tools.
safety: Skip chemical drain cleaner; it burns skin and eats old pipes.
If you already poured cleaner in, wear gloves and eye protection.

steps.instruction: Pull the drain stopper straight up
details: Push the stopper down first, then pull.
If it won't come, turn it a quarter turn and pull again.
steps.check: The stopper is out of the drain in your hand.

steps.instruction: Pull the hair off the stopper
details: Use a paper towel, it's gross but quick.
Look down the drain with a flashlight for more.
steps.check: The stopper and its rod are clean.

steps.instruction: Run hot water for one minute
details: Hot tap water rinses the soap out.
Never use boiling water on plastic pipes.
steps.check: Water goes straight down the open drain.

steps.instruction: Drop the stopper back in
details: Some stoppers have a slot: turn it so the rod catches.
steps.check: The stopper sits in the drain and moves up and down with the rod.

steps.instruction: Test: run the water for 30 seconds
details: Pull the stopper rod up so the drain is open.
steps.check: No water stays in the bowl.

problems.title: Still slow after cleaning the stopper
symptoms: Still slow after cleaning the stopper

plan.diagnosis: With the stopper clean, the clog is further down in the U-shaped P-trap under the sink, where gunk settles. It comes off by hand with two big plastic nuts, so you can empty it into a bucket.
safety: If you used chemical drain cleaner, wear gloves and goggles: the trap water is caustic.

steps.instruction: Open the cabinet and clear it out
details: Move everything out from under the sink.
steps.check: You can see the white U-shaped pipe.

steps.instruction: Put a bucket under the U-bend
details: Water will pour out when it comes off.
steps.check: The bucket sits right under the U-bend.

steps.instruction: Unscrew both big nuts by hand
details: Turn them toward you, counterclockwise from above.
Use pliers with a towel only if they're stuck.
steps.check: Both nuts are loose and slide along the pipe.

steps.instruction: Pull the U-bend down and empty it
details: Tip it into the bucket.
Expect a bad smell; that's normal.
steps.check: The U-bend is off and empty.

steps.instruction: Put the U-bend back and hand-tighten the nuts
details: Check the thin washers are still inside the nuts.
Hand-tight is enough; too tight cracks them.
steps.check: Both nuts are snug and the trap doesn't wiggle.

steps.instruction: Run water and look for drips
details: A drip means a nut needs a quarter turn more.
steps.check: Water drains fast and no drips fall into the bucket.

problems.title: Weak water from the faucet
symptoms: Water barely comes out of the faucet
Low water pressure at the sink

plan.diagnosis: Little bits of minerals and grit collect in the aerator, the screen at the tip of the faucet, and choke the stream. Unscrewing it and rinsing it out brings the pressure back.

steps.instruction: Close the drain so nothing falls in
details: The aerator has small parts; a towel over the drain works too.
steps.check: The stopper is down.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the faucet tip by hand
details: Turn it to the right, looking down from above.
If it's stuck, wrap a cloth around it and use pliers gently.
steps.check: The aerator is off in your hand.

steps.instruction: Rinse the grit out of the screen
details: Tap it on the counter and rinse it under another tap.
White crust soaks off in vinegar in 30 minutes.
steps.check: You can see clean holes in the screen.

steps.instruction: Screw the tip back on
details: Keep the little parts in the same order.
steps.check: It's snug and doesn't leak.

steps.instruction: Turn the water on full
details: Still weak? The valves under the sink may be half closed.
steps.check: A strong, even stream comes out.

problems.title: Still weak with a clean aerator
symptoms: Still weak with a clean aerator

plan.diagnosis: With a clean aerator, the next most likely cause is a shutoff valve under the sink that got bumped or half closed. Opening both fully brings full pressure back.
safety: If a valve drips when you turn it, close it back and call a plumber.

steps.instruction: Open the cabinet under the sink
steps.check: You can see two small valves on the wall.

steps.instruction: Turn both valves all the way open
details: Counterclockwise opens them.
Don't force a valve that won't move; call a plumber.
steps.check: Both handles stop turning counterclockwise.

steps.instruction: Test the faucet on hot and cold
steps.check: Both run strong.

problems.title: Leaking under the sink
symptoms: The cabinet under the sink is wet

plan.diagnosis: Most drips under a bathroom sink come from a loose plastic nut on the drain trap, which works loose over time. Finding the drip and snugging that nut by hand fixes it.
safety: If water sprays from a supply hose, close its shutoff valve right away.

steps.instruction: Open the cabinet and dry everything
details: Starting dry makes the drip easy to find.
steps.check: The pipes and the cabinet floor are dry.

steps.instruction: Put a bucket under the pipes
steps.check: The bucket is under the trap.

steps.instruction: Run water and find the first drip
details: Feel each joint with a dry paper towel.
Water on the supply hoses or valves is a different leak.
steps.check: You can point at where the drip starts.

steps.instruction: Snug the leaking nut by hand
details: A quarter turn past hand-tight at most.
steps.check: The nut is snug.

steps.instruction: Run water again and check it's dry
details: Still dripping at a valve or hose? Close the valve and call a plumber.
steps.check: No more drips.
